category: AC/DC Module: Electrostatics, Electric Currents, Shells and Circuit Elements
description: Domain, boundary, edge and point features of the Electrostatics (es), Electric Currents (ec) and Electric Currents in (Layered) Shells (ecis) interfaces, their AC/DC Module couplings, and the device/element nodes of the Electrical Circuit (cir) interface, as documented in the COMSOL 6.4 AC/DC Module User's Guide. Java type strings were verified against the 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Free Space (AC/DC domain feature)
tools.description: Default domain node of Electrostatics, Magnetic Fields, Magnetic Fields, No Currents, Magnetic Field Formulation, Magnetic and Electric Fields and the machinery interfaces that models vacuum or air around a device (epsilon_r = 1, mu_r = 1, zero conductivity). It is the canvas on top of which material-specific nodes (Charge Conservation, Ampère's Law, Magnet, Coil...) are added, and it needs no material. If the selection covers materials that are inconsistent with vacuum, those materials are ignored and a solver warning is issued unless the physics-level consistency check is switched off.
tools.usage: Added automatically as the first domain node of the interface; Model Builder: <interface> > Free Space 1. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("mf").feature("fsp1") (type FreeSpace; mfco/mmtp use the tag 'free')

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains treated as free space; override locally with other domain nodes further down the tree.

parameters.name: Stabilization (Magnetic Fields)
parameters.description: Free-space stabilization conductivity used to keep frequency-domain/time-domain A-formulations well posed in nonconducting regions.

parameters.name: Check applicability of features in study
parameters.description: Physics-level setting; clearing it disables the material-consistency check.

tools.notes: New in the 6.x AC/DC interfaces (earlier versions used Charge Conservation / Ampère's Law with air material). Application Library: ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/inductor_3d.

tools.name: Zero Charge (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Default exterior boundary condition of Electrostatics that sets n·D = 0, i.e. no displacement field crosses the boundary; it is also the correct condition on symmetry planes where the potential is symmetric. On interior boundaries it decouples the two sides so the potential can be discontinuous. Use Ground/Electric Potential/Terminal on electrodes and keep Zero Charge on the outer air box when the box is large enough.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Zero Charge (default on exterior boundaries). Java: physics("es").create("zc2", "ZeroCharge", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Exterior or interior boundaries; exterior boundaries get it by default.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("es").feature("zc1").selection().all();  // default node
// Electrostatics, Boundary Elements has the same node (types ZeroCharge / ZeroChargeEdge)
tools.notes: For open-field problems prefer an Infinite Element Domain or the esbe interface rather than a small box with Zero Charge. Symmetry Plane (for Electric Field) offers explicit symmetric/antisymmetric choices.

tools.name: Space Charge Density (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Domain source that adds a volume charge density rho_v (C/m^3) to the right-hand side of Gauss' law, div D = rho_v. Use it for fixed ionized dopant charge, beam space charge computed elsewhere, electrolyte charge or charge densities coupled from Semiconductor/Transport of Charge Carriers models. Default value 0 C/m^3; supports Harmonic Perturbation.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Domains > Space Charge Density. Java: physics("es").create("scd1", "SpaceChargeDensity", 3); feature("scd1").set("rhoq", "...")

parameters.name: rhoq
parameters.description: Space charge density rho_v (SI unit C/m^3), default 0.

parameters.name: harmonicPerturbation
parameters.description: Marks the contribution as a small-signal perturbation.

tools.notes: Used in Semiconductor_Module/Quantum_Systems/schrodinger_poisson_nanowire and Electric_Discharge_Module/Streamer_Discharges/double_headed_streamer_discharge_chemistry. For particle beams use the Electric Particle-Field Interaction coupling instead.

tools.name: External Surface Charge Accumulation (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Boundary condition that sets the surface charge rho_s from a distributed ODE, d(rho_s)/dt = n·J_i + n·J_e, where the normal ion and electron current densities are user inputs (typically from a plasma or charged-particle model). It lets charge build up on dielectric surfaces in time-dependent discharge, DBD and charging simulations without solving the plasma inside the same interface.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Boundaries > External Surface Charge Accumulation (time-dependent studies)

parameters.name: Normal ion current density n·J_i
parameters.description: Incident ion current density (A/m^2).

parameters.name: Normal electron current density n·J_e
parameters.description: Incident electron current density (A/m^2).

parameters.name: Material type
parameters.description: Solid, Nonsolid or From material (matters on deforming meshes).

tools.example: Electrostatics > External Surface Charge Accumulation on the dielectric wall; set n·J_i = cpt.bnd1.Jin (from Charged Particle Tracing wall accumulator) and n·J_e = 0; solve Time Dependent.
tools.notes: Not supported by the D-V formulation. The Plasma interface has its own Surface Charge Accumulation node for plasma-adjacent dielectrics.

tools.name: Electric Displacement Field (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Boundary condition that prescribes the normal component of the electric displacement field, n·D = n·D0. Use it to impose a known flux of D (for example derived from an analytical gate model or an adjacent region that is not meshed) instead of a potential or a surface charge.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Boundaries > Electric Displacement Field. Java: physics("es").create("df1", "DisplacementField", 2); feature("df1").set("D0", new String[]{...})

parameters.name: D0
parameters.description: Boundary electric displacement field vector (C/m^2).

tools.notes: Application Library: Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/si_inversion_layer_density_gradient_and_schrodinger_poisson.

tools.name: Thin Low Permittivity Gap (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Interior-boundary condition that represents a thin layer of thickness d and small relative permittivity (air gap, adhesive film, oxide) between two dielectric domains without meshing it; the normal displacement across the boundary is related to the potential jump through epsilon_r/d. Default thickness 5 mm, epsilon_r from material.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Boundaries > Thin Low Permittivity Gap. Java: physics("es").create("tcl1", "ThinLowPermittivityGap", 2); set("d", "1[mm]"); set("epsilonrbnd", "1")

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Gap thickness (default 5 mm).

parameters.name: epsilonrbnd
parameters.description: Relative permittivity of the gap material (From material or user defined).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Introductory_Electrostatics/thin_low_permittivity_gap_comparison compares the node with a fully resolved gap.
tools.notes: Only valid when the gap permittivity is much lower than the neighbours'. For a thin high-permittivity sheet use Dielectric Shielding; the magnetic analogue is Thin Low Permeability Gap.

tools.name: Dielectric Shielding (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Boundary condition modelling a thin sheet of high-permittivity dielectric of thickness ds that conducts displacement flux tangentially along the surface (a tangential Gauss' law on the boundary). It replaces a thin domain and saves mesh elements, e.g. dielectric coatings, grading layers and thin insulating films with large epsilon_r.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Boundaries > Dielectric Shielding. Java: physics("es").create("des1", "DielectricShielding", 2); set("ds", "1[mm]")

parameters.name: ds
parameters.description: Surface thickness of the sheet (default 1 m, set it explicitly).

parameters.name: epsilonr
parameters.description: Relative permittivity of the sheet (From material, taken from adjacent domains if not set).

parameters.name: Material type
parameters.description: Solid / Nonsolid / From material.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Introductory_Electrostatics/dielectric_shielding_comparison: coating on an electrode modelled as a boundary vs. a resolved domain.
tools.notes: Electric Currents counterpart: Electric Shielding (conductive sheet). Low-permittivity sheets need Thin Low Permittivity Gap instead.

tools.name: Distributed Capacitance (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Exterior boundary condition for a thin dielectric sheet or film (relative permittivity epsilon_r, thickness ds) connected on its far side to a reference potential Vref, so n·D = epsilon0*epsilon_r*(Vref - V)/ds. Use it for thin insulating coatings on grounded electrodes, oxide layers over a back plane, or capacitive sensors whose dielectric film is too thin to mesh.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Boundaries > Distributed Capacitance

parameters.name: epsilon_r
parameters.description: Relative permittivity of the sheet.

parameters.name: ds
parameters.description: Surface thickness (default 1 mm).

parameters.name: Vref
parameters.description: Reference potential behind the sheet (default 0 V).

tools.example: Capacitive touch sensor: apply Distributed Capacitance (epsilon_r = 4, ds = 0.5 mm, Vref = 0) on the cover-glass underside instead of meshing the glass.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library; record a macro or Save as Java to obtain it. Electric Currents analogue: Distributed Impedance.

tools.name: Line Charge / Point Charge (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Lower-dimensional charge sources: Line Charge applies Q_L (C/m) along 3D edges, Line Charge (Out-of-Plane) applies it at 2D points, Line Charge (on Axis) on the symmetry axis in 2D axisymmetry; Point Charge applies Q_P (C) at 3D points (Point Charge (on Axis) in 2D axisymmetry). Both support Harmonic Perturbation. Use them for thin wires, idealized charged filaments and point sources in field computations.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Edges > Line Charge; Points > Point Charge / Line Charge (Out-of-Plane)

parameters.name: Q_L
parameters.description: Line charge per unit length (C/m), default 0.

parameters.name: Q_P
parameters.description: Point charge (C), default 0.

tools.example: High-voltage line over ground (2D): Points > Line Charge (Out-of-Plane) with Q_L = 2*pi*epsilon0_const*V0/log(2*h/r0) at the conductor position.
tools.notes: Fields are singular at the source; evaluate away from it. Constraining the potential on edges/points instead gives mesh-dependent charge.

tools.name: Electrostatic Point Dipole (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Point source in 2D and 3D representing the limit of two opposite point charges with vanishing separation and fixed dipole moment p (C·m), directed from the negative to the positive charge. Specify either Magnitude and direction or the full Electric dipole moment vector. Useful for molecular dipoles, EEG/ECG equivalent sources in dielectrics and small polarized particles.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Points > Electrostatic Point Dipole

parameters.name: Dipole specification
parameters.description: Magnitude and direction (default) or Electric dipole moment.

parameters.name: n_p, p
parameters.description: Direction vector and magnitude of the dipole moment.

tools.example: Place a point in a spherical head model, add Electrostatic Point Dipole with p = 1e-8 C·m along z, solve Stationary and plot es.normE.
tools.notes: Electric Currents has the analogous Electric Point Dipole (current dipole, A·m). Supports Harmonic Perturbation.

tools.name: Charge Conservation, Ferroelectric (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Electrostatics domain node for ferroelectric materials with nonlinear, optionally hysteretic polarization, normally used together with the Electrostriction coupling and Solid Mechanics in the Ferroelectroelasticity multiphysics interface. Polarization models include Langevin and hyperbolic-tangent anhysteretic curves and a Jiles–Atherton-type electric hysteresis (parameters Psat, alpha, a, k, c). Requires the MEMS, Structural Mechanics or Acoustics Module.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Charge Conservation, Ferroelectric (added by Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Electrostriction > Ferroelectroelasticity). Java: physics("es").create("ccnfe1", "ChargeConservationFerroelectric", 3)

parameters.name: PolarizationModel
parameters.description: LangevinFunction or HyperbolicTangent anhysteretic curve.

parameters.name: Hysteresis
parameters.description: Enable electric hysteresis (Jiles–Atherton parameters alphaJAe, aJAe, kJAe, cJAe, chie0).

parameters.name: Psat
parameters.description: Saturation polarization (e.g. 0.425 C/m^2 in the library model).

parameters.name: EffectiveField
parameters.description: Use total field or a user-defined effective field.

tools.example: Application Libraries MEMS_Module/Piezoelectric_Devices/piezoelectric_hysteresis (P-E and butterfly loops, Batch Sweep) and MEMS_Module/Actuators/electrostrictive_disc (Charge Conservation, Ferroelectric + Electrostriction coupling).
tools.notes: Use with time-dependent or quasi-static parametric studies; hysteresis requires small load steps.

tools.name: Charge Conservation, Piezoelectric (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Electrostatics domain node paired with a Piezoelectric Material node in Solid Mechanics through the Piezoelectric Effect coupling; the constitutive data (coupling matrix, permittivity at constant strain) are locked to the solid-mechanics node when the coupling is active. Without an active coupling the domain behaves as a dielectric with epsilon_rS. Added automatically by the Piezoelectricity, Solid multiphysics interface.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Charge Conservation, Piezoelectric. Java: physics("es").create("ccnp1", "ChargeConservationPiezo", 3); multiphysics().create("pze1", "PiezoelectricEffect", 3)

parameters.name: epsilonrS
parameters.description: Relative permittivity at constant strain (used only when unlocked).

parameters.name: coordinateSystem
parameters.description: Material orientation (e.g. rotated system for cut crystals).

parameters.name: Dispersion / Conduction Loss subnodes
parameters.description: Dielectric and conductive losses in frequency-domain analyses.

tools.example: Application Library MEMS_Module/Piezoelectric_Devices/piezoceramic_tube and aln_lamb_wave_resonator_3d (Eigenfrequency + Frequency Domain with terminal admittance es.Y11).
tools.notes: Requires MEMS, Structural Mechanics or Acoustics Module. See also Piezoelectricity (multiphysics interface) and Piezoelectric Effect entries.

tools.name: Dispersion (Electrostatics / Electric Currents)
tools.description: Subnode of Charge Conservation, Charge Conservation, Piezoelectric and Current Conservation that adds frequency-dependent dielectric polarization (dielectric loss) in Eigenfrequency, Frequency Domain and Time Dependent studies. Material models: Debye (default), Multipole Debye, Cole–Cole, Havriliak–Negami, Constant Loss Tangent and User defined, with optional temperature shift functions (WLF, Arrhenius). Since 6.3 several Dispersion subnodes are additive, so multipole models can be built up.
tools.usage: Charge Conservation (or Current Conservation) > right-click > Dispersion. Java: feature("ccn1").create("ddis1", "DebyeDispersion", 3); set("MaterialModel", "DebyeModel")

parameters.name: MaterialModel
parameters.description: DebyeModel, Multipole Debye, Cole–Cole, Havriliak–Negami, Constant loss tangent, User defined.

parameters.name: tauv / Gv
parameters.description: Relaxation time(s) and relative permittivity contribution(s) (default 1 us, 100).

parameters.name: shiftFunction
parameters.description: none, WLF (Twlf, C1wlf, C2wlf) or Arrhenius (T0, Q) temperature shift.

parameters.name: StaticResponse
parameters.description: Low-frequency or high-frequency interpretation of the parent permittivity.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ec").feature("cucns1").create("ddis1", "DebyeDispersion", 3);
model.component("comp1").physics("ec").feature("cucns1").feature("ddis1").set("tauv", new String[]{"1[us]"});
tools.notes: Present by default in many library models (e.g. ACDC_Module/Devices,_Capacitive/capacitor_transient, high_voltage_insulator). Time-domain use adds auxiliary polarization DOFs.

tools.name: Conduction Loss (Time-Harmonic) (Electrostatics)
tools.description: Subnode of Charge Conservation that adds conductive loss sigma*E to a dielectric in Eigenfrequency and Frequency Domain studies only, so piezoelectric or dielectric resonators get a finite Q from leakage current. Conductivity can be From material, User defined (isotropic to full tensor) or Linearized resistivity (rho0, alpha, Tref). Requires the Acoustics, MEMS or Structural Mechanics Module.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Charge Conservation > right-click > Conduction Loss (Time-Harmonic)

parameters.name: Electric conductivity sigma
parameters.description: From material, User defined or Linearized resistivity.

parameters.name: Temperature (model input)
parameters.description: Used by the linearized resistivity model.

tools.example: Quartz or PZT resonator: add Conduction Loss (Time-Harmonic) with sigma = 1e-9 S/m under Charge Conservation, Piezoelectric and compare the admittance peak width.
tools.notes: Has no effect in Stationary or Time Dependent studies; use Electric Currents for DC leakage.

tools.name: D-V Formulation (Electrostatics discretization option)
tools.description: Mixed formulation of the Electrostatics interface that solves for both the electric displacement field D and the potential V (instead of V only), giving a more accurate D/charge in highly heterogeneous or ferroelectric media. It is selected in the interface's Discretization section and is available in 2D and 3D with an AC/DC or MEMS license. Pair features, Surface Charge Accumulation, External Surface Charge Accumulation and a spatially varying Change Thickness are not supported.
tools.usage: Electrostatics > Settings > Discretization > Formulation: D-V formulation (enable Show More Options > Advanced Physics Options if hidden)

parameters.name: Formulation
parameters.description: V-formulation (default) or D-V formulation.

parameters.name: Out-of-plane thickness
parameters.description: Only a global constant value is supported with D-V in 2D.

tools.example: Ferroelectric capacitor with strongly nonlinear polarization: switch the Electrostatics discretization to D-V formulation and re-solve the Batch Sweep for a smoother P-E loop.
tools.notes: Theory: 'Theory for the Electrostatics Interface with the D-V Formulation' in the AC/DC User's Guide.

tools.name: Domain Terminal (Electrostatics / Electric Currents)
tools.description: Domain-level version of the Terminal node: the whole selected domain (a conductor that is not meshed internally in a meaningful way) is held at one potential, excited by Voltage, Charge (es), Current (ec), Circuit, Power or Terminated with a reference impedance. Its terminal name indexes the capacitance/admittance matrices produced by Stationary Source Sweep or terminal sweeps. Convenient for metal parts such as fittings and electrodes modelled as volumes.
tools.usage: Electrostatics / Electric Currents > Domains > Terminal (label 'Domain Terminal'). Java: physics("es").create("term1", "DomainTerminal", 3); set("TerminalType", "Voltage"); set("V0", "1")

parameters.name: TerminalName
parameters.description: Numeric name used as index in es.C11, es.Y21 ... matrices.

parameters.name: TerminalType
parameters.description: Voltage, Charge (Electrostatics), Current (Electric Currents), Circuit, Power, Terminated.

parameters.name: V0 / Q0 / P0
parameters.description: Excitation value.

parameters.name: Zref / CharacteristicImpedanceFrom
parameters.description: Reference impedance for Terminated terminals and S-parameters.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Capacitive/high_voltage_insulator: 'Metal Fitting, Line End' domain terminal at V0 and 'Metal Fitting, Ground End' grounded.
tools.notes: Boundary Terminal (type Terminal) is catalogued separately as 'Terminal'. Domain selection removes the domain's interior equation; voltages are uniform.

tools.name: Harmonic Perturbation (AC/DC excitation subnode)
tools.description: Subnode of Terminal, Electric Potential, Coil, Metal Contact, Edge Current, Normal Current Density and other sources that defines the small AC part of an excitation for a Small-Signal Analysis, Frequency Domain (Stationary + Frequency-Domain Perturbation) study, while the parent holds the DC bias. Exclusive-type subnodes replace the parent value in the perturbation step; contributing-type subnodes add to it. Coil versions accept a coil current or coil voltage (default 1 A / 1 V).
tools.usage: Right-click the source node > Harmonic Perturbation (Physics toolbar > Attributes). Java: feature("term1").create("hp1", "HarmonicPerturbation", 2); for coils feature("coil1").create("hp1", "CoilHarmonicPerturbation", -1)

parameters.name: V0 / I0 / Q0
parameters.description: Perturbation amplitude of the terminal quantity.

parameters.name: ICoil / VCoil
parameters.description: Coil current or voltage perturbation (CoilHarmonicPerturbation).

parameters.name: Study step
parameters.description: Only active in Frequency-Domain Perturbation (type Frequencylinearized) steps.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/small_signal_analysis_of_inductor: DC coil current 30 A, Harmonic Perturbation ICoil = 1 A, frequency sweep of the differential inductance mf.LCoil_1.
tools.notes: Evaluate small-signal results with lindev()/linper(); the MEMS biased resonator and semiconductor MOSCAP C-V models use the same mechanism.

tools.name: Electric Scalar–Scalar Potential Coupling (es–esbe)
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling that enforces continuity of the electric potential across boundaries between a finite-element Electrostatics interface and an Electrostatics, Boundary Elements interface, so detailed dielectric parts are meshed with FEM while the surrounding infinite air is handled by BEM. The coupling is unnecessary if both interfaces use the same dependent-variable name.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Electric Scalar–Scalar Potential Coupling (available when es and esbe are both present)

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Manual or All boundaries (FEM/BEM interface boundaries).

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Electrostatics (FEM) and Electrostatics, Boundary Elements.

tools.example: Capacitive sensor with a ceramic substrate: es on the substrate, esbe on the air region, coupling on the substrate surface; use right preconditioning with iterative solvers.
tools.notes: Magnetic analogues: Magnetic Scalar–Scalar Potential Coupling (mfco/mfncbe) and Magnetic Vector–Scalar Potential Coupling (mf/mfncbe).

tools.name: Archie's Law (Electric Currents conductivity subnode)
tools.description: Subnode available when the parent Current Conservation (or similar) uses Archie's law for the electric conductivity. It computes the effective conductivity of a nonconductive porous matrix saturated by a conducting fluid, sigma = S_L^n * eps_p^m * sigma_L, from the fluid conductivity, cementation exponent m, saturation exponent n, saturation S_L and porosity eps_p. Typical uses: geoelectrics, soil and rock resistivity, groundwater and borehole logging models.
tools.usage: Current Conservation > Electric conductivity: Archie's law, then right-click > Archie's Law

parameters.name: sigma_L
parameters.description: Fluid electric conductivity (From material or user defined).

parameters.name: m
parameters.description: Cementation exponent.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Saturation exponent.

parameters.name: S_L / eps_p
parameters.description: Fluid saturation and porosity.

tools.example: Resistivity survey (ACDC_Module/Devices,_Resistive/geoelectrics style): brine conductivity 5 S/m, porosity 0.2, m = 2, n = 2, S_L = 1.
tools.notes: Also available in Electrostatics/Magnetic interfaces for the corresponding material parameter where supported.

tools.name: Effective Medium (AC/DC material mixture subnode)
tools.description: Subnode that computes an effective electric conductivity, relative permittivity or relative permeability of a mixture of up to five materials with given volume fractions, when the parent node's material parameter is set to Effective medium. Three mixing rules are offered for each property: Volume average of the property (upper bound, 'parallel'), Volume average of its reciprocal (lower bound, 'series', e.g. resistivity) and a Power law in between. Typical uses are composites, porous media and powders.
tools.usage: Current Conservation / Charge Conservation / Ampère's Law > set parameter to Effective medium > right-click > Effective Medium

parameters.name: Number of materials
parameters.description: Up to 5 constituents.

parameters.name: Material i
parameters.description: Domain material or any material from the Materials node.

parameters.name: Volume fraction theta_i
parameters.description: Fractions between 0 and 1, normally summing to 1.

parameters.name: Effective property model
parameters.description: Volume average (property), Volume average (reciprocal property) or Power law.

tools.example: Carbon-black filled polymer: Effective Medium with polymer (0.9) and carbon (0.1) using the Power law rule for conductivity in Electric Currents.
tools.notes: Theory: 'Effective Material Properties in Effective Media and Mixtures' in the AC/DC User's Guide.

tools.name: Current Conservation in Solids / Fluids (Electric Currents)
tools.description: Main domain node of Electric Currents that solves div J = Qj with J = sigma*E + dD/dt + Je. In 6.4 it exists in two variants, Current Conservation in Solids (material-frame properties) and Current Conservation in Fluids (spatial-frame properties), replacing the old Material type setting. The Jc-E relation can be From material, User defined, Effective medium, Archie's law, Hall effect (stationary only) or Linearized resistivity, and the D-E relation Relative permittivity, Polarization, Remanent electric displacement, Dielectric losses, Loss tangent (loss angle or dissipation factor) or Dispersion; the Fluids variant supports only Relative permittivity and Polarization.
tools.usage: Electric Currents > Current Conservation (default). Java: physics("ec").create("cucns1", "CurrentConservationSolid", 3); set("ConstitutiveRelationJcE", "LinearizedResistivity")

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationJcE
parameters.description: ElectricalConductivity, LinearizedResistivity, HallEffect (HallCoef, B from model input), Effective medium, Archie's law.

parameters.name: sigma / rho0, alpha, Tref
parameters.description: Conductivity tensor or linearized-resistivity data.

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationDE
parameters.description: RelativePermittivity, Polarization or Dispersion.

parameters.name: Model inputs
parameters.description: Temperature, magnetic flux density (Hall effect).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Capacitive/hall_effect_sensor: Hall effect constitutive relation with B from an mfnc model.
tools.notes: Current Conservation in Fluids was introduced in 6.4 (versions 6.3 and earlier used Material type Solid/Nonsolid).

tools.name: Current Source (Electric Currents)
tools.description: Domain source that adds a distributed current source Qj (A/m^3) to the continuity equation. It deliberately violates current conservation locally, so use it with care, e.g. to represent injection from an electrochemical or biological process that is not otherwise modelled. Supports Harmonic Perturbation.
tools.usage: Electric Currents > Domains > Current Source

parameters.name: Qj
parameters.description: Current source density (A/m^3), default 0.

tools.example: Neural tissue model: Current Source Qj = I_stim/V_region in a small electrode region with a return Ground elsewhere.
tools.notes: Prefer Terminal/Normal Current Density on boundaries for physical electrodes. Line and point variants: Line Current Source, Point Current Source.

tools.name: Normal Current Density (Electric Currents)
tools.description: Exterior boundary source/sink condition: either Inward current density -n·J = Jn (positive means current flowing into the domain) or a full Current density vector J0 whose normal component is applied. Use it for distributed current injection when the total current (Terminal) or potential is not the natural specification.
tools.usage: Electric Currents > Boundaries > Normal Current Density. Java: physics("ec").create("ncd1", "NormalCurrentDensity", 2); set("nJ_type", "nJ"); set("nJ", "1[A/cm^2]")

parameters.name: nJ_type
parameters.description: Inward current density (nJ) or Current density (J0).

parameters.name: nJ / J0
parameters.description: Value(s), default 0.

parameters.name: harmonicPerturbation
parameters.description: Enable small-signal contribution.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/mosfet_with_explicit_metal_and_dielectric couples semi.nJ into the ec metal regions with Normal Current Density.
tools.notes: Also available in the Magnetic and Electric Fields interface.

tools.name: Distributed Impedance (Electric Currents)
tools.description: Exterior boundary condition for a thin resistive (and, in AC/transient, capacitive) sheet connecting the domain to a reference potential Vref: n·J = (sigma/ds + i*omega*epsilon0*epsilon_r/ds)(V - Vref) in frequency domain. The layer is given either as Thin layer (ds, sigma, epsilon_r) or as Surface impedance (surface resistance rho_s and capacitance C_s). Use it for electrode contact layers, coatings and skin-electrode interfaces.
tools.usage: Electric Currents > Boundaries > Distributed Impedance

parameters.name: Vref
parameters.description: Reference potential (default 0 V).

parameters.name: Layer specification
parameters.description: Thin layer (default ds = 5 mm, sigma, epsilon_r From material) or Surface impedance (rho_s, C_s).

tools.example: ECG electrode on skin: Distributed Impedance with rho_s = 1e-2 ohm*m^2 and C_s = 0.1 F/m^2 to a reference potential of the electrode.
tools.notes: Interior counterpart: Contact Impedance. Supports exclusive Harmonic Perturbation.

tools.name: Electric Shielding (Electric Currents)
tools.description: Boundary condition for a thin highly conductive sheet (thickness ds, conductivity sigma, optional permittivity) that carries tangential current along the surface, replacing a thin domain to reduce the mesh. Displacement currents in the sheet are included in Frequency Domain and Time Dependent studies. Typical uses: metallization, foil shields, heating films and PCB copper on a thick insulating substrate.
tools.usage: Electric Currents > Boundaries > Electric Shielding. Java: physics("ec").create("es1", "ElectricShielding", 2); set("ds", "35[um]")

parameters.name: ds
parameters.description: Surface thickness (default 1 cm).

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: Sheet conductivity (Conduction Current section as in Current Conservation).

parameters.name: epsilonr
parameters.description: Sheet relative permittivity for AC/transient.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Introductory_Electric_Currents/electric_shielding and electric_shielding_comparison; ACDC_Module/Electromagnetic_Heating/igbt_joule_heating uses it for bond metallization.
tools.notes: Also available in Electric Currents, Single Layer Shell. For multilayer sheets prefer the Electric Currents in Layered Shells interface.

tools.name: Contact Impedance (Electric Currents)
tools.description: Interior (or pair) boundary condition representing a thin resistive layer between two conducting domains; the normal current is proportional to the potential jump, n·J1 = (V1 - V2)/rho_s. Specify it as Thin layer (ds, sigma, epsilon_r) or Surface impedance (rho_s, C_s); frequency-domain and transient studies also include the layer capacitance. Also available as Pair Contact Impedance and in the Magnetic and Electric Fields interface.
tools.usage: Electric Currents > Boundaries > Contact Impedance (Pairs > Pair Contact Impedance). Java: physics("ec").create("ci1", "ContactImpedance", 2); set("spec_type", "thinlayer"); set("ds", "1[cm]")

parameters.name: spec_type
parameters.description: thinlayer or surface impedance.

parameters.name: ds, sigmabnd, epsilonrbnd
parameters.description: Layer thickness (default 5 mm), conductivity and permittivity.

parameters.name: rhos, Csr
parameters.description: Surface resistance (ohm*m^2) and capacitance for the surface-impedance option.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Introductory_Electric_Currents/contact_impedance_comparison: resolved oxide layer vs. Contact Impedance.
tools.notes: For rough mechanical contacts use Electrical Contact (Cooper–Mikic–Yovanovich correlations).

tools.name: Electrical Contact (Electric Currents)
tools.description: Interior or pair condition giving the electrical conductance h of two bodies in imperfect contact due to surface roughness, n·J = h(V1 - V2). The constriction conductance comes from the Cooper–Mikic–Yovanovich correlation (plastic), the Mikic elastic correlation, or a user-defined h_c, with asperity height/slope, contact pressure and hardness (microhardness, Vickers or Brinell). Pair with Thermal Contact for electro-thermal switch and connector analysis.
tools.usage: Electric Currents > Boundaries > Electrical Contact (Pairs > Pair Electrical Contact)

parameters.name: Constriction conductance
parameters.description: Cooper–Mikic–Yovanovich (default), Mikic elastic, or User defined h_c.

parameters.name: sigma_asp, m_asp
parameters.description: Asperity average height (default 1 um) and slope (default 0.4).

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: Contact pressure (often from Solid Mechanics contact: solid.Tn).

parameters.name: Hardness
parameters.description: Microhardness H_c (default 3 GPa), Vickers (c1, c2) or Brinell.

tools.example: Bolted busbar joint: Pair Electrical Contact with p = solid.Tn from a contact analysis, sigma_asp = 1 um, m_asp = 0.4.
tools.notes: Theory: 'Theory for Electrical Contact' in the AC/DC User's Guide.

tools.name: Sector Symmetry (Electric Currents / Rotating Machinery)
tools.description: Pair condition used at the sliding interface between rotating and stationary parts when only a sector of the machine is modelled; it maps the potential between pair source and destination with a sector count n_sect (< 50) and Continuity or Antiperiodicity. It must be combined with Periodic Condition features on the radial sector boundaries (at least two, one per side). In 2D rotation is about the origin.
tools.usage: Pairs > Sector Symmetry (Electric Currents, Rotating Machinery, Magnetic, Magnetic Fields). Java: physics("rmm").create("ssc1", "SectorSymmetry", 2)

parameters.name: Number of sectors n_sect
parameters.description: Default 2.

parameters.name: Type of periodicity
parameters.description: Continuity or Antiperiodicity.

parameters.name: Axis of rotation a_rot
parameters.description: Rotation axis vector (3D).

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Pointwise (default), weak or Nitsche constraints.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/pm_motor_3d: one pole pitch with Sector Symmetry on the air-gap identity pair.
tools.notes: Use a finer mesh on the destination side of nonconforming pairs. The Arkkio Torque Calculation can use Sector Symmetry boundaries automatically.

tools.name: Line / Point Current Source and Electric Point Dipole (Electric Currents)
tools.description: Lower-dimensional current sources for Electric Currents: Line Current Source Q_j (A/m) on 3D edges or 2D points (on-axis variant in 2D axisymmetry), Point Current Source Q_j (A) on 3D points, and Electric Point Dipole, a current source–sink pair of moment p (A·m) specified by magnitude and direction or as a vector. Used for electrodes much smaller than the domain (geophysical surveys, stimulation needles, EEG source models).
tools.usage: Electric Currents > Edges > Line Current Source; Points > Point Current Source / Electric Point Dipole. Java: physics("ec").create("pcs1", "PointCurrentSource", 0); set("Qjp", "1[A]")

parameters.name: Qjl / Qjp
parameters.description: Line current per length (A/m) or point current (A).

parameters.name: Dipole specification
parameters.description: Magnitude and direction or Dipole moment for Electric Point Dipole.

parameters.name: harmonicPerturbation
parameters.description: Small-signal contribution flag (point source).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Resistive/geoelectrics: Point Current Source with Qjp = +1 A / -1 A at the two current electrodes of a Wenner array.
tools.notes: Potentials are singular at the source; measure away from it or use probe averaging.

tools.name: Change Cross Section / Change Thickness (Out-of-Plane) (AC/DC)
tools.description: Local overrides of the interface-level cross-section area (1D components) or out-of-plane thickness (2D components) for specific geometric entities, so that lumped quantities such as terminal current, capacitance and resistance are computed with the correct extent. The default unit area/thickness otherwise makes the 1D/2D equation identical to a 3D slice of unit size.
tools.usage: Electrostatics / Electric Currents > Change Cross Section (1D) or Change Thickness (Out-of-Plane) (2D)

parameters.name: Cross-section area A
parameters.description: 1D components (default one unit area).

parameters.name: Thickness d
parameters.description: 2D components; overrides the interface Out-of-plane thickness locally.

tools.example: 2D busbar cross-section of two different lamination stack heights: Change Thickness d = 20 mm on one domain group and 35 mm on the other so ec.I0_1 is correct.
tools.notes: Change Thickness is not supported with the D-V formulation.

tools.name: Electric Currents in Layered Shells (ecis)
tools.description: Boundary interface (3D faces) for current, field and potential in thin and thick conductive shells and dielectric layers with an internal layered structure; it is the layered-by-default twin of Electric Currents in Shells (both use tag ecis and Java type ElectricCurrentsShell). The potential can live on the surface or in a product space with an extra dimension through the thickness, allowing normal potential variation inside and between layers defined by Layered Material nodes. Studies: Stationary, Frequency Domain, Time Dependent, Eigenfrequency; inductive effects are neglected (skin depth >> device).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > AC/DC > Electric Fields and Currents > Electric Currents in Layered Shells. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ecis", "ElectricCurrentsShell", "geom1")

parameters.name: Shell type
parameters.description: Layered shell (default here) or Nonlayered shell.

parameters.name: Layered Material / Layered Material Link
parameters.description: Defines layer thicknesses, materials and extra-dimension mesh (lne elements per layer).

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Conductive Shell, Electric Insulation, Initial Values; add Terminal (Interface Terminal), Ground, Insulating Layer, Interlayer Connection.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/planar_pcb_coil, ACDC_Module/Introductory_Electric_Currents/solid_multilayer_shell_comparison and ACDC_Module/Electromagnetic_Heating/heating_circuit.
tools.notes: Replaces the legacy Electric Currents, Single Layer Shell (ecs) and Electric Currents, Layered Shell (ecls) interfaces. Combine with Layered Shell (structural) for piezoelectric/piezoresistive layered couplings.

tools.name: Conductive Shell (Electric Currents in Shells)
tools.description: Default boundary node of Electric Currents in (Layered) Shells that adds the current-continuity equation for the shell potential and defines conductivity and permittivity of each layer. In layered mode the Layer model is General (full through-thickness 3D representation) or Highly conductive layer (potential constant through the thickness, more stable for thin metal layers).
tools.usage: Electric Currents in Shells > Conductive Shell. Java: physics("ecis").create("csh1", "ConductiveShell", 2); set("LayerType", "General")

parameters.name: LayerType / LayerTypeNonLS
parameters.description: General or HighlyConductiveLayer.

parameters.name: shelllist / applyTo
parameters.description: Layered material link and which layers/interfaces (all, top, bottom) are selected.

parameters.name: lth, lne
parameters.description: Thickness and number of extra-dimension elements when no layered material is used.

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationJcE / DE
parameters.description: Conductivity and permittivity models as in Current Conservation.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/planar_pcb_coil: Cu layers as Conductive Shell, FR4 as Insulating Layer.
tools.notes: Piezoresistive Shell extends this node for piezoresistivity couplings (MEMS Module).

tools.name: Insulating Layer / Dielectric Layer (Electric Currents in Shells)
tools.description: Layer-selective nodes of Electric Currents in (Layered) Shells: Insulating Layer removes the physics from selected layers so no current flows through them (e.g. a PCB core), while Dielectric Layer (layered shells only) solves Gauss' law in the selected layers with a given permittivity, turning them into a local electrostatics problem. Layers are chosen with the Layer and Interface Selection tools of the linked Layered Material.
tools.usage: Electric Currents in Shells > Insulating Layer (type InsulatingLayer) / Dielectric Layer. Java: physics("ecis").create("inl1", "InsulatingLayer", 2)

parameters.name: shelllist / shelllist_lCheck
parameters.description: Layered material link and which layers are affected.

parameters.name: epsilon_r (Dielectric Layer)
parameters.description: Relative permittivity of the dielectric layers.

tools.example: Two-layer flex circuit: copper top/bottom as Conductive Shell, polyimide middle layer as Dielectric Layer to capture interlayer capacitance in a Frequency Domain study.
tools.notes: See Interlayer Connection to electrically short selected layers along edges (vias).

tools.name: Interlayer Connection (Electric Currents in Shells)
tools.description: Edge feature of the layered shell interfaces that removes the potential gradient in the thickness (extra-dimension) direction for the selected layers, so their tops and bottoms share one potential and they are electrically connected. Several Interlayer Connection nodes create separate connected groups; on a single layer it converts the full 3D formulation into an in-plane conservation problem, which is numerically more stable for thin highly conductive layers.
tools.usage: Electric Currents in Shells > Edges > Interlayer Connection

parameters.name: Layer selection
parameters.description: Layers (from the Layered Material) to connect.

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Advanced Physics Options.

tools.example: Model a via between top and bottom copper of a PCB trace: Interlayer Connection on the via edge with both copper layers selected.
tools.notes: The legacy ecls interface has a similar Interlayer Connection and a Homogenized Shell Connection.

tools.name: Piezoelectric Layer (Electric Currents in Layered Shells)
tools.description: Extension of Dielectric Layer for piezoelectric films in layered shells, used with the Piezoelectricity, Layered multiphysics coupling and a Piezoelectric Material node in the structural Layered Shell interface. Added automatically by the Piezoelectricity, Layered Shell multiphysics interface; requires the Structural Mechanics, MEMS or Acoustics Module (plus Composite Materials for layered shells).
tools.usage: Electric Currents in Layered Shells > Piezoelectric Layer. Java: physics("ecis").create("epzml1", "PiezoelectricLayer", 2); multiphysics().create("pzel1", "PiezoelectricEffectLS", 2)

parameters.name: shelllist / applyTo
parameters.description: Layered material and piezoelectric layers selected.

parameters.name: epsilonrS
parameters.description: Permittivity at constant strain (locked when coupled).

parameters.name: weakConstraints
parameters.description: Constraint handling at interfaces with conductors.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Electromagnetics_and_Mechanics/piezoelectric_layered and MEMS_Module/Piezoelectric_Devices/aln_lamb_wave_resonator_layered.
tools.notes: Electrodes are modelled with Interface Terminal / Ground on layer interfaces.

tools.name: Electric Currents Solid to Shell Via Boundary (coupling)
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling that enforces continuity of the electric potential between an Electric Currents (solid) interface and an Electric Currents in Shells / Layered Shells interface on shared boundaries, so volumetric conductors can feed thin layered films. Useful for solder joints or bond wires meshed as solids attached to PCB copper modelled as shells.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Electric Currents Solid to Shell Via Boundary (available when ec and ecis are present)

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Boundaries where the solid and shell connect.

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Electric Currents and Electric Currents in (Layered) Shells.

tools.example: Power module: bond wires in ec (3D domains) connected to DBC copper traces in ecis via this coupling; add Electromagnetic Heating for a Joule-heating analysis.
tools.notes: Listed in 'Overview of Multiphysics Couplings' of the AC/DC Module.

tools.name: Electric Currents, Single Layer Shell (ecs) / Layered Shell (ecls) – legacy interfaces
tools.description: Legacy shell interfaces that can still be opened and solved but no longer added: Electric Currents, Single Layer Shell (ecs; 2D edges and 3D faces; stationary, frequency, small-signal and time domain; nodes Current Conservation, Change Shell Thickness, Normal Current Density, Electric Shielding) and Electric Currents, Layered Shell (ecls; 3D, stationary; Layered Shell and Homogenized Shell features with Varying Thickness, Interlayer and Homogenized Shell Connections). Both are replaced by Electric Currents in Shells / Electric Currents in Layered Shells (ecis).
tools.usage: Open existing models; for new work use AC/DC > Electric Fields and Currents > Electric Currents in (Layered) Shells

parameters.name: Homogenized Shell
parameters.description: Integrates conductivities of selected layers through the thickness (parallel resistors) for an in-shell problem.

parameters.name: Layered Shell
parameters.description: Resolves potential through the thickness with the extra dimension.

tools.example: To migrate: add ecis, reproduce the layer stack with a Layered Material, map Current Conservation -> Conductive Shell and Homogenized Shell -> Conductive Shell with Highly conductive layer.
tools.notes: The existing catalog entry 'Electric Currents in Shells (ecs)' refers to the modern interface, whose tag in 6.4 is ecis.

tools.name: Subcircuit Definition / Subcircuit Instance (Electrical Circuit)
tools.description: Subcircuit Definition groups circuit elements into a reusable block with named pins (and optional input parameters), and Subcircuit Instance inserts that block into the main circuit, mapping its pins to circuit nodes in the order the pins were defined. Subcircuits are also what SPICE .SUBCKT statements are imported into.
tools.usage: Electrical Circuit > Subcircuit Definition (add elements as subnodes) and Subcircuit Instance. Java: physics("cir").create("sub1", "SubCircuitBlock", -1); physics("cir").create("X1", "SubCircuit", -1); feature("X1").set("subCircuitName", "sub1")

parameters.name: Pin names (Connections of SubCircuitBlock)
parameters.description: Ordered list of subcircuit pins, e.g. p, n, out.

parameters.name: subCircuitName
parameters.description: Definition referenced by the instance.

parameters.name: Connections (instance)
parameters.description: Main-circuit node for each pin.

parameters.name: parameters / paramValues
parameters.description: Instance-specific input parameters (Advanced Physics Options).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Electromagnetics_and_Circuits/opamp_capacitive_load: op-amp macromodel as Subcircuit Definition 'OPAMP' with instance XOPAMP driving a capacitive load.
tools.notes: Elements inside a subcircuit may connect only to its pins and to each other.

tools.name: External I vs. U / External U vs. I (Electrical Circuit)
tools.description: Circuit elements that embed a finite-element device into the circuit. External I vs. U takes a voltage from a field model (a Circuit-type terminal, lumped port or multiturn coil) as a voltage source between two nodes and feeds the resulting circuit current back as the field model's current excitation; External U vs. I does the opposite (field model current in, circuit voltage back). Coils, Terminals, Lumped Ports and Metal Contacts set to Circuit type appear in their Voltage/Current lists.
tools.usage: Electrical Circuit > External I vs. U / External U vs. I. Java: physics("cir").create("IvsU1", "ModelDeviceIV", -1); feature("IvsU1").set("V", "mf.VCoil_1"); setIndex("Connections", "2", 0, 0)

parameters.name: Connections
parameters.description: Two node names; the first is the positive reference terminal.

parameters.name: V (External I vs. U)
parameters.description: Voltage source variable from the field model or user defined.

parameters.name: I (External U vs. I)
parameters.description: Current variable from the field model.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/inductor_3d: coil with Circuit (current) excitation connected through External I vs. U to a voltage source and resistor; ecore_transformer uses two of them.
tools.notes: For inductive/wave models the voltage must be a line integral (coil or port voltage), not a single-point potential; use External I-Terminal only for electrostatic/electric-current terminals.

tools.name: External I-Terminal (Electrical Circuit)
tools.description: Circuit element that assigns a voltage-to-ground measured at a Circuit-type terminal of another physics interface (Electric Currents, Electrostatics, Semiconductor, piezoelectric models) to a single circuit node, and returns the node current to that terminal as a current excitation. It is the simplest way to put a resistive/capacitive/piezo device between a circuit node and ground.
tools.usage: Electrical Circuit > External I-Terminal. Java: physics("cir").create("termI1", "ModelTerminalIV", -1); feature("termI1").set("V", "ec.V0_1"); setIndex("Connections", "1", 0, 0)

parameters.name: Connections
parameters.description: Single node name.

parameters.name: V
parameters.description: Terminal voltage variable (listed automatically for circuit-type terminals).

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Electromagnetics_and_Circuits/circuit_fem_resistor and MEMS_Module/Piezoelectric_Devices/piezoelectric_energy_harvester (harvester electrode connected to a load resistor).
tools.notes: Not valid for inductive or wave problems; use External I vs. U there.

tools.name: SPICE Circuit Import / Export (Electrical Circuit)
tools.description: Right-click actions of the Electrical Circuit node: Import Spice Netlist translates a Berkeley-SPICE .cir netlist into Electrical Circuit nodes (the first line is treated as the title and ignored; statements are case-insensitive), and Export Spice Netlist writes the compatible circuit nodes back to a .cir file. Supported statements are R, C, L, V, I, E, F, G, H, D, Q, M and X, plus .model, .subckt (becomes a Subcircuit Definition) and .include. Use it to bring vendor models (op-amps, diodes, transistors) into a multiphysics model or to hand a circuit to an external simulator.
tools.usage: Model Builder > Electrical Circuit > right-click > Import Spice Netlist / Export Spice Netlist (default extension .cir)

parameters.name: Filename
parameters.description: SPICE netlist file (.cir).

parameters.name: Device statements
parameters.description: R, C, L, V, I, E/F/G/H controlled sources, D (diode), Q (NPN/PNP BJT), M (n/p MOSFET), X (subcircuit instance).

parameters.name: Dot commands
parameters.description: .model (resolves device type/parameters), .subckt, .include.

tools.example: Import an op-amp macromodel netlist, then connect its output node to an External I vs. U element driving a coil in Magnetic Fields.
tools.notes: Unsupported SPICE commands are skipped; check the Messages window after import.

tools.name: BJT / MOSFET / Diode device models (Electrical Circuit)
tools.description: Large-signal semiconductor device elements of the Electrical Circuit interface: NPN BJT and PNP BJT (collector/base/emitter; parameters such as IS, BF (default 100), BR, NF, NC, CJE, CJC, IKF, RB), n-Channel and p-Channel MOSFET (drain/gate/source/bulk; VTO, KP, GAMMA, PHI, LAMBDA, W, L, overlap and junction capacitances) and Diode (p/n; IS, N, RS, CJO, VJ, M, BV, TNOM). Defaults are reasonable but manufacturer model cards should be used for real parts.
tools.usage: Electrical Circuit > NPN BJT / PNP BJT / n-Channel MOSFET / p-Channel MOSFET / Diode. Java: physics("cir").create("D1", "Diode", -1); physics("cir").create("Q1", "BjtNpn", -1)

parameters.name: Connections
parameters.description: Device node names (e.g. Collector|Base|Emitter).

parameters.name: IS, N, RS, CJO, VJ, BV
parameters.description: Diode model parameters.

parameters.name: BF, BR, IS, CJE, CJC, RB
parameters.description: BJT model parameters.

parameters.name: VTO, KP, W, L, LAMBDA (MOSFET)
parameters.description: Threshold voltage (0 V), transconductance (2e-5 A/V^2), gate width/length (50 um) and channel-length modulation (see 'MOSFET Transistors' theory).

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/pn_diode_circuit compares a circuit Diode with a full Semiconductor diode; ACDC_Module/Electromagnetics_and_Circuits/inductor_in_circuit uses an NPN BJT.
tools.notes: Type strings for PNP and MOSFET elements were not found in the 6.4 library; record them with Save as Java if needed.

tools.name: Mutual Inductance / Transformer (Electrical Circuit)
tools.description: Mutual Inductance couples two existing Inductor elements with coupling factor k (0-1, default 0.98), giving M = k*sqrt(L1*L2). Transformer is a four-node element that is either two coupled inductors (Specify inductors: k, L1, L2, defaults 0.98, 1 mH, 1 mH) or an Ideal transformer with winding ratio N1/N2 (default 10).
tools.usage: Electrical Circuit > Mutual Inductance / Transformer

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Coupling factor.

parameters.name: L1, L2
parameters.description: Inductor features (Mutual Inductance) or inductance values (Transformer).

parameters.name: Transformer model
parameters.description: Specify inductors or Ideal transformer (N1/N2).

tools.example: Flyback converter test bench: Transformer (k = 0.99, L1 = 200 uH, L2 = 20 uH) between a Switch-driven primary and a Diode/Capacitor secondary.
tools.notes: For field-accurate coupling use two Coil features with External I vs. U elements instead of an idealized transformer.

tools.name: Switch (Electrical Circuit)
tools.description: Two-node element that connects or disconnects a path when conditions are met: Voltage controlled, Current controlled or Custom expressions, each with separate On and Off conditions (On true when the expression > 0, Off true when < 0). The state changes only on a false-to-true transition of a condition (allowing Schmitt-trigger and latch behaviour); in the on state it has an On resistance, in the off state no current flows, and a Switching time smooths the transition. It triggers implicit events that update a discrete _state variable in Time Dependent studies.
tools.usage: Electrical Circuit > Switch

parameters.name: Connections
parameters.description: Two node names.

parameters.name: Switch condition
parameters.description: Voltage controlled, Current controlled or Custom expressions.

parameters.name: On / Off condition
parameters.description: Expressions in sens.v (voltage) or sens.i (current); on when > 0, off when < 0.

parameters.name: Initial state
parameters.description: Use on condition, Use off condition or Boolean expression.

parameters.name: On resistance / Switching time
parameters.description: Conduction resistance in the on state and transition time.

tools.example: Contactor model: Switch closes when t > 5 ms (custom expression t-5[ms]) connecting the coil (External I vs. U) to a 24 V source.
tools.notes: Use strict/intermediate time stepping around switching instants for accuracy.

tools.name: Controlled Sources and Meters (Electrical Circuit)
tools.description: Dependent sources Voltage-Controlled Voltage Source (E), Voltage-Controlled Current Source (G), Current-Controlled Voltage Source (H) and Current-Controlled Current Source (F), specified by a gain with sense pins (or a general expression), plus the Voltmeter and Ampère Meter measurement elements. They build amplifiers, behavioural models and probe signals inside circuit networks.
tools.usage: Electrical Circuit > Voltage-Controlled Voltage Source (type VoltageVoltageSource) / ... / Voltmeter (type VoltMeter) / Ampère Meter

parameters.name: Connections
parameters.description: Output nodes (and sense nodes).

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: gain (with gainPosSensePin/gainNegSensePin) or expression.

parameters.name: gain / expr
parameters.description: Gain value or controlling expression.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Electromagnetics_and_Circuits/opamp_capacitive_load: VCVS EGAIN with gain OPAMP_GAIN and a Volt Meter on the output.
tools.notes: Current-controlled sources use the current flowing through one or more two-pin devices, with a Use gain (gain in ohm for CCVS) or Custom expression method.
